articles.title: Previewing New England’s Week 9 Matchup vs. the Green Bay Packers | Patriots Roundtable Podcast
articles.summary: The New England Patriots return home for a prolific matchup against the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium on Sunday evening. We preview the game on today...
articles.body:
Check out the Patriots Roundtable Podcast for more!

This Sunday, the New England Patriots (5-3) return to the comfort of Gillette Stadium for one of their most premier matchups of the 2026 regular season: an interconference showdown with the Green Bay Packers (5-3). New England's second game against NFC North opponents this fall is ripe with intrigue on the field and on the sidelines, setting up for one of the most entertaining bouts of the year league-wide.

On today's episode of the Patriots Roundtable Podcast, hosts Eddie Marotta and Tyler Geis preview the Patriots' upcoming home stand against Green Bay — examining matchups that could swing the game's result, keys to victory on both sides of the football, and predicting the game's outcome.

On the sidelines, all eyes will be fixed on two New England legends. Tom Brady makes his return to Foxboro on the FOX broadcast, and Rob Gronkowski will be inducted into the Patriots' Hall of Fame as part of the weekend's festivities.

Between the white lines, Sunday's matchup pits two teams with eerily similar identities against each other. Drake Maye and Jordan Love are both quarterbacks who have excelled at threatening defenses with downfield passing, while each team's defensive structure is built upon taking away those opportunities for their opponents.

For New England's offense, it will be another in a string of games where the health of key skill position players will be closely monitored. A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson have continued to miss practice time, and have now been joined by Hunter Henry — who was limited to just eight offensive snaps before suffering a foot injury in Week 8. Those absences didn't seem to matter much for Maye and the passing attack, however, as the third-year gunslinger continued his recent excellence with another efficient performance that featured two 40-yard passing touchdowns. He'll need to carry that success over into this weekend, while the offense as a whole will look to limit the turnovers that have plagued them against a defense that leads the league in takeaways.

On the defensive side of the football, the Patriots' secondary will be challenged by an equally aggressive passing offense. Love leads all quarterbacks with 52 attempts on passes 20-plus yards downfield, and has the tools along the boundary to create explosive plays in an instant. Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, and Tucker Kraft each present stylistically different predicaments for New England's coaching staff to gameplan for, but that's been a strength so far this season. Much like the Patriots, the Packers have struggled to find consistency on the ground — ranking at or near the bottom of the league in nearly every rushing statistical or analytical category.

This will be a game that places a heavy emphasis on quarterback play on both sides — strategies that have served both teams well through eight weeks of the regular season. Who remains standing by the end of the evening could come down to one final possession, or who can force the opposition into critical mistakes. For New England, they'll look to create those errors, rather than being forced to overcome them — an internal battle that's yet to be resolved.

articles.title: Ben James produces another low round and takes the 36-hole lead in Mexico
articles.summary: Ben James posted another sub-65 round to grab the 36-hole lead by one shot at El Cardonal.
articles.body:
LOS CABOS, Mexico — Ben James ran off five straight birdies around the turn and finished with an aggressive tee shot for one last birdie and an 8-under 64 on Friday to build a one-shot lead going into the weekend at the World Wide Technology Championship.

James, already assured his PGA Tour card for next year as the No. 1 player in the PGA Tour University ranking, had his 14th round of 65 or lower in 13 tournaments since turning pro out of Virginia this summer.

He already has four finishes in the top 5 and picking up plenty of experience along the way. A victory would put him on the Championship Series under the new model in 2028 and move him into the top 50 in the world.

"It's weird, in college I was kind of someone that would shoot 2, 3 under every time out and would have trouble going low," James said. "But you adapt to your surroundings as humans, so I guess out here that's what you have to do. I've been rolling it well and playing well, so nice to be shooting some low numbers."

James was at 15-under 129 at the Tiger Woods-designed El Cardonal at Diamante. He was one shot ahead of Peter Malnati, who was tied for the lead until coming up short of the green on the par-3 ninth and missing a 12-foot par putt to end his round of 64.

"I work really hard on my game and I haven't had tons to show for that lately," Malnati said. "So to not be in that position coming down the stretch on a Friday where ... I don't even have to think about the cut line, I can think about playing golf. That was fun."

Zac Blair had a 68 and was three shots behind.

This is the second time James has had the lead going into the weekend. The other was the RBC Canadian Open, and he shot a 78 to quickly spiral out of contention. He also had a good chance to win the Biltmore Championship Asheville until Jacob Bridgeman put on a putting clinic down the stretch in the final round.

"I'm doing everything right," James said. "But for me, I'm just trying to win each shot, just do the best I can for each golf shot and not thinking ahead and just do the best I can. And as I say, winning the shot at hand."

He won the par-5 18th when he least expected it. James has been relying on his short wedges, and hit a pedestrian pitch to about 18 feet. But he holed the putt, and then started the front nine with three straight birdies to set the target.

This is among the last three tournaments of the FedEx Cup Fall, after which the top 100 players keep full status for next year.

articles.title: Tiger Woods and ex-wife Elin Nordegren reunite to celebrate son Charlie's college golf commitment
articles.summary: Tiger Woods and ex-wife Elin Nordegren reunited at their son Charlie Woods' high school to celebrate his Florida State University golf commitment.
articles.body: It was a family reunion for Charlie Woods on Friday, as both his father and mother, whose divorce was highly publicized, were together again to celebrate his college commitment. Woods, the son of 15-time major winner Tiger, announced earlier this year his commitment to play golf at Florida State University. The Woods family, including Tiger's ex-wife, Elin Nordegren, were on hand at Charlie's high school to celebrate. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Tiger and Elin got divorced after the former's infidelity had been exposed. Charlie announced the commitment in February. "Excited to announce my commitment to play golf at Florida State University — go Noles!" he wrote. "Congratulations Charlie. I'm so proud of you on entering this next chapter of your life," Tiger commented. It is a rare public appearance for Tiger, who has remained out of the spotlight most of the time since he was arrested in March. LIV GOLF IS OFFICIALLY OVER AFTER ANNOUNCING PLANS TO 'WIND-DOWN' OPERATIONS AFTER FAILED RESCUE DEAL He was arrested on charges of DUI following a car crash in which police later found hydrocodone pills in his pocket. Law enforcement proceeded to perform field sobriety tests because of their suspicions. Woods was instructed to remove his eyeglasses, and the deputy conducting the tests stated that his eyes appeared to be "bloodshot and glassy" and "extremely dilated." articles.title: Two main parties neck and neck after New Zealand vote, early count
articles.summary: Early results suggests New Zealand’s National and Labour parties polling just short of 30 percent of the popular vote.
articles.body:
New Zealand’s ruling centre-right National Party and main opposition Labour have both secured just short of 30 percent of the popular vote, with just 27 percent of the election results counted.

The Electoral Commission on Saturday showed the current three-party ruling coalition led by National would have a majority of just one seat, after an election dominated by a struggling economy and voter disillusionment with the two biggest contenders.

It added that the centrist Opportunity Party will meet the 5 percent threshold to enter parliament, potentially becoming a kingmaker.

Polling stations opened at 9am on Saturday (20:00 GMT Friday) and closed at 7pm (06:00 GMT Saturday).

New Zealand’s Electoral Commission aims to release preliminary results from 95 percent of polling stations by the end of election night on Saturday. A final result, which will reflect ballots cast by New Zealanders abroad, is expected by November 27.

There is no timeframe for when a government must be formed.

New Zealand’s 2026 election has been at times dubbed the “supermarket election”, where grocery prices and supermarket competition have become a key battleground for political parties.

Peter Dunne, a former member of New Zealand’s parliament, who also served as a minister in both National and Labour-led governments, said that the election is “much more of a cost-of-living election”, with voters essentially looking at “which of the main blocs is better placed to ease the cost of living burden on New Zealanders”.

“The ruling coalition appears well ahead of the centre-left. Now, that may change because these are early results, but it’s a little bit of a surprise that this is happening,” Dunne told Al Jazeera. “We were looking to a much tighter contest than appears to be the case at the moment.”

The National Party pledged to return the budget to surplus through fiscal discipline while expanding the national pension scheme. The Labour Party promised cheaper healthcare and transport.

The former minister added that both main parties are practically “carbon copies of the other”, leaving “a whole rising generation of voters, who want to see a bit more adventure in politics”.

Dunne said that, therefore, the results show support rallying behind other parties, like “strong support for the Green Party, the right-wing libertarian [ACT New Zealand], the xenophobic nationalist [New Zealand First] party, and a new centrist party, the Opportunity Party, which wants to be in the middle between all of them”.

He told Al Jazeera that even though the Opportunity Party is currently hovering around 5 percent at the moment – also the threshold for representation in parliament – “it’s been one of the big stars of this campaign”.

New Zealand holds a general election every three years under a mixed-member proportional system.

Voters do not elect a leader of the country, but instead select a local electorate candidate and a political party.

Dunne told Al Jazeera that if both main parties of the blocs “end up relatively evenly placed, then the onus could go on the Opportunity Party”.

“If Opportunity Party reaches parliament, it will talk to the largest party first, which appears to be the National Party, but there’s no guarantee that they could come to an arrangement,” he said.

“We could face weeks of interparty negotiations to form a government. Parliament has to sit by early January, so there’s a real prospect that we could go into Christmas with no clear government in New Zealand,” Dunne added.

Electorate winners earn a seat in the typically 120-seat parliament, as do the highest-ranked members of the party, based on their national party vote.

All votes are counted by hand, not by machine.

articles.title: Jon Rahm leads Abu Dhabi Championship with Rory McIlroy among challengers going into final round
articles.summary: John Rahm leads on 18 under, one clear of Tyrell Hatton and Francesco Laporta in tie for second; Rory McIlroy, chasing record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, is 16 under; final round of Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, live on Sky Sports Golf from 6.30am on Sunday
articles.body:
McIlroy, chasing a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, and coming off the back of carding a career-high 11 birdies in his second round, had shared the lead at one stage before bogeying the par-three 17th.

McIlroy's five-under 67 also included a double-bogey six at the 10th, which interrupted a streak of seven birdies from the Northern Irishman between holes seven and 14.

Rahm sits on 18 under after a six-under 66 on Saturday at Yas Links GC, one clear of Hatton and Laporta who each carded a 67.

Adam Scott continued his bogey-free tournament with a 66 to sit 15 under in fifth place, one shot behind McIlroy.

It leaves three Masters champions in the top five of the leaderboard, with Rahm (2023), McIlroy (2025, 2026) and Scott (2013) all in the mix going into the final day.

The two-week playoffs on the DP World Tour saw 70 players enter the $9m Abu Dhabi Championship before the 50 top-ranked players advance to the $10m finals event in Dubai next week.

McIlroy is currently projected to rise to No 2 in the Road to Dubai rankings, behind Eugenio Chacarra who fired a five-under 67 on Saturday to find himself tied for 29th in Abu Dhabi at eight under.

articles.summary: El de Barrika borda el sábado y retrasa a McIlroy, que achucha al líder de la Race to Dubai
articles.body: En la economía colaborativa que este fin de semana protagoniza el deporte español, Alcaraz mete a Jódar en las Finales ATP y Jon Rahm impulsa las opciones de victoria de Eugenio López-Chacarra para ser campeón del DP World Tour la próxima semana en Dubái como sólo entre los españoles hizo él en 2019 y Seve Ballesteros en seis ocasiones. En un sábado soleado en Abu Dabi, sin viento severo y banderas para hacer resultado si se era preciso, Jon bordó el golf en los segundos nueve hoyos. Los despachó en 31 golpes, con tres birdies y un eagle -un putt de 9 metros-, para firmar un rotundo 66, uno más que horas antes había firmado Ángel Ayora, protagonista de una buena escalada en el día del movimiento, cuya recompensa final puede ser en siete días un billete para el PGA Tour. El joven de San Roque compartió con Ding la mejor vuelta del día. (Resultados) Anunció a comienzos de semana Jon, que había dedicado más tiempo a los biberones que a los hierros en este mes y medio largo, que su juego estaba oxidado, pero bastó el contacto con Yas Links, un campo que premia al que coge calle más que otros, para cogerle el pulso otra vez y plantarse a falta de 18 hoyos con 18 bajo par y con un golpe de ventaja sobre su antiguo compañero en la extinta Legión XIII, Tyrrell Hatton y el italiano Francesco Laporta. Sobre todo fue en los segundos nueve donde hizo la vuelta. Estuvo algo dubitativo en el inicio, pero supo aprovechar los dos pares 5 para paliar el bogey del hoyo 4 (par 3) porque no cogió el green. Sacarle partido a los hoyos largos, faceta que en torneos a veces le cuesta al vizcaíno, es un condicionante grande en campos como el del Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship. Aquí en tres días acumula -11 en 12 hoyos.Se le escapó por medio palmo el del 18, a la caída de la tarde, para haber ampliado más distancia. Mientras, Rory Mcilroy, que ha ganado cinco veces en el desierto, pero no en este emirato, tiró 67 golpes y es cuarto a dos de Jon. El norirlandés, el número 2 del mundo, persigue su octava Orden de Mérito ahora llamada Race to Dubái con Chacarra como principal adversario. Rory lleva 25 birdies en Abu Dhabi. Nunca había hecho tantos en el DP World Tour tras el sábado. Un doble bogey en el 10 le birló el liderato. El madrileño, mientras, olvidó los problemas con el driver que había tenido esta semana y firmó otro 67 para ascender hasta el vigésimo noveno puesto. Chacarra lamentó que algún bogey, como el del 15, se produjese después de haber pegado el segundo golpe desde el centro de la calle, pero acabó satisfecho y derrochando humildad. "Me he dado cuenta cuando jugué con Rory el jueves que hay 36 jugadores por delante de mí en el ránking y que tengo que seguir trabajando y mejorar para llegar donde está él". Si se mantienen en ese tono el domingo, el español saldrá en Dubái con unos 600 puntos sobre McIlroy. Un colchoncito sin ser nada definitivo.

articles.title: Abu Dhabi Championship: Jon Rahm takes one-shot lead into final round
articles.summary: Jon Rahm leads Tyrrell Hatton and Francesca Laporta by one shot, and Rory McIlroy by two, after the third round of the Abu Dhabi Championship.
articles.body:
Abu Dhabi Championship third-round leaderboard

18 J Rahm (Spa); -17 T Hatton (Eng), F Laporta (Ita); -16 R McIlroy (NI); -15 A Scott (Aus); -14 M Jordan (Eng), D Puig (Spa)

Selected others: -12 S Bairstow (Eng), N Kimsey (Eng); -11 T Fleetwood (Eng), E Ferguson (Sco), A Sullivan (Eng); -9 A Rai (Eng); -8 E Chacarra (Spa), M Wallace (Eng); -1 P Reed (US)

Jon Rahm has a one-shot lead going into the final round of the Abu Dhabi Championship but Ryder Cup team-mates Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy are in close contention.

The 31-year-old Spaniard shared the overnight lead with Italy's Francesco Laporta and fellow former LIV player Hatton, but moved clear of them both with a six-under-par 66 at Yas Links on Saturday.

Hatton and Laporta both carded a 67, as did McIlroy, who goes into the final round in fourth place on 16 under.

Rahm, who said recently that he does not know what 2027 holds after quitting the LIV tour, is aiming for a first solo tournament triumph since winning the Masters in 2023.

Reigning Masters champion McIlroy remains in hot pursuit, however, after bouncing back in spectacular fashion since being given a two-shot penalty in the opening round for improving his lie before taking a chip shot.

The six-time major winner hit 11 birdies in a second-round 63 and another eight in his third round, but a double bogey six at the par-four 10th - and another dropped shot at the 17th - left McIlroy two shots off the lead.

And he acknowledges that it will take something special on the final day to reel in Rahm and co.

"There are low ones [scores] out there and I am going to have to shoot a low one - something in the mid to low 60s - to get it done tomorrow and that will be the goal," said McIlroy.

Hatton, meanwhile, is looking forward to going head-to-head again with Rahm after playing alongside the two-time major champion, and Laporta, in Saturday's final group.

All three will play together once again on Sunday.

"Obviously final group tomorrow there's a lot to play for," said Hatton, who briefly moved level with Rahm at the top of the leaderboard in the third round after holing his seventh birdie of the day on the 14th.

"Naturally we are going to want to beat each other. Hopefully I can get off to a good start and put him under some pressure."

Rahm, who is chasing his first win in the Abu Dhabi Championship, responded well after being put under pressure by Hatton on Saturday.

He reclaimed the outright lead on the 15th with a superb, curling 20-foot birdie putt and came close to extending his advantage at the last, just coming up short with another birdie chance as he finished without a single dropped shot.

Laporta also produced a bogey-free round to keep pace with the field's big hitters as the 36-year-old, who shot 10 under par to claim a first-round lead, bids for a first title on the DP World Tour.

Elsewhere, Australian Adam Scott remained bogey-free for the tournament after three rounds and moved up to fifth place on 15 under with a 66.

And Englishman Matthew Jordan is a shot further back, alongside Spain's David Puig, after a third-round 69.

articles.title: Jiří Klíma's late goals not enough as Beavers fall to Bowling Green
articles.summary: Nov. 7—BOWLING GREEN, Ohio — Bowling Green had the strongest of starts and never looked back. Just 15 seconds into Friday's series opener, the Bemidji State...
articles.body:
Nov. 7—BOWLING GREEN, Ohio — Bowling Green had the strongest of starts and never looked back.

Just 15 seconds into Friday's series opener, the Bemidji State men's hockey team fell behind 1-0 when Brody Waters finished Brayden Crampton's one-time pass. Three minutes and 12 seconds later, Ty Higgins scored a shorthanded goal on a tight-angle shot to put Bowling Green ahead 2-0.

The Falcons sat on the early cushion, then padded the lead to hand the Beavers their first CCHA loss of the season, 5-2.

BGSU sat on the two-goal lead until the final minutes of the second period. Brandon Whynott tapped home a pass from Dominik Rymon with 82 seconds left before the intermission. Waters added his second goal of the night three and a half minutes into the third period.

Jiří Klíma got the Beavers back into the game with a pair of goals 49 seconds apart. He converted on BSU's sixth and final power play of the night, with assists from Max Namestnikov and Oliver Peer. Klíma then beat goaltender Jacob Steinman five-hole to pull Bemidji State within two.

Connor Levis silenced the comeback effort with his empty-net goal with 1:35 left in regulation. The Beavers fell to 2-5-1 (1-1-1 CCHA), while the Falcons (5-4) remained a perfect 3-0 in league games.

Steinman finished with 27 saves on 29 shots. Max Hildebrand stopped 20 shots for BSU. The Beavers filled off six of their seven penalties, including 38 seconds of a 5-on-3 in the second period.

articles.title: Kanpur hit-and-run: Speeding Thar kills man, drags body for 20 metres; 2 women, man flee
articles.summary: 55-year-old scooter rider killed in Kanpur’s Kalyanpur after speeding Thar hit and dragged him; SUV seized, CCTV being reviewed, probe underway.
articles.body: KANPUR: A 55-year-old man riding a scooter was killed after a speeding, out-of-control Thar rammed into him in Awas Vikas-3, Kalyanpur area of Kanpur, on Saturday evening. The SUV dragged the victim and his scooter for nearly 20 metres before crashing into a green belt outside a house.The deceased was identified as Santosh Singh Chauhan, a resident of Panki. His son, Rahul Chauhan, said his father had left home saying he would return shortly.Eyewitnesses said two young women and a man travelling in the Thar screamed after the crash and later left the spot in another car.Police also recovered two helmets from the accident site.Police have taken the body into custody and sent it for postmortem. Kalyanpur station in-charge Keshav Tiwari said the SUV was seized and CCTV footage from the area was being collected as part of the investigation.Residents said the Thar first hit the scooter rider, then crashed into a house before ramming the boundary wall of another nearby house. articles.title: House scores 30 as Furman defeats Northern Iowa 98-83
articles.summary: (AP) — Tom House scored 30 points as Furman beat Northern Iowa 98-83 on Saturday.House shot 9 for 14 (7 for 11 from 3-point range) and 5 of 6 from the free-t...
articles.body:
GREENVILLE, S.C. (AP) — Tom House scored 30 points as Furman beat Northern Iowa 98-83 on Saturday.

House shot 9 for 14 (7 for 11 from 3-point range) and 5 of 6 from the free-throw line for the Paladins (3-0). Abijah Franklin scored 21 points and added seven rebounds. Luka Toews had 14 points and shot 3 for 6 (1 for 3 from 3-point range) and 7 of 8 from the free-throw line.

Isaiah Johnson-Arigu led the way for the Panthers (1-1) with 20 points and two blocks. Northern Iowa also got 17 points and two steals from Carson Vis. Greyson Uelmen also had 15 points, eight rebounds, four assists and two steals.

Furman took the lead with 15:46 remaining in the first half and did not trail again. House led his team in scoring with 11 points in the first half to help put them up 44-31 at the break. House scored a team-high 19 points in the second half.

Furman plays Wednesday against Holy Cross on the road, and Northern Iowa hosts Green Bay on Tuesday.

articles.title: Scan to pay, burst by clock, breathe by bulletin: Delhi-NCR's Diwali, 10 years on
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The shopkeeper is still wrapping your diya, and your phone has already buzzed with the payment confirmation.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The shopkeeper is still wrapping your diya, and your phone has already buzzed with the payment confirmation.A decade ago, the same festive shopping run in Delhi-NCR meant cash in hand, a round of bargaining and a string of small payments at the neighbourhood shop. The rituals are still here. Almost everything around them has changed: how people pay, what they are allowed to burst, how cities prepare and how the air is measured.In its November 2, 2026 order, the Supreme Court has allowed certified green crackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8, but only between 6am and 7am and between 8pm and 10pm. The complete ban returns from November 9.Also Read|Delhi’s Diwali-eve air quality worst in 10 years; AQI set to worsen moreSince Diwali 2016, UPI has grown from a newly launched payment system into a daily habit. Courts have rewritten the rules of celebration, and air quality has become a standing item on the festive calendar. Official records from 2016 and 2025, along with this year's orders, show how much has changed, and where the record goes silent. How UPI took over the festive shopping bagThe clearest shift is in how people pay.UPI was launched on August 25, 2016, with 21 banks. By FY2025-26, 703 banks were live on the network, according to the PIB's release marking UPI's tenth year.The growth is steeper still. The PIB release says annual UPI transactions rose from 1.78 crore in FY2016-17 to 24,161.69 crore in FY2025-26. Transaction value went from Rs 0.07 lakh crore to about Rs 314 lakh crore.In calendar year 2025 alone, UPI processed about 22,000 crore transactions, roughly 60 crore a day, according to the government release. Person-to-merchant transactions made up 63% of UPI volume in the first half of 2025, and 86% of these were below Rs 500.That points to everyday, small-value retail payments, the kind a festival is full of.Diwali 2016 fell within UPI's first year. The figures above are national numbers, not Diwali sales data, so they cannot tell us how much festive spending has moved from cash to digital. They do show the scale of the payment system that now sits behind much of the festival's commerce.How crackers became a Supreme Court matterThe rules around firecrackers have changed just as dramatically.In November 2016, in the Arjun Gopal case, the Supreme Court suspended licences for the sale of firecrackers in Delhi-NCR. It was the start of sustained judicial intervention in the festival. The court returned to the issue, and in its October 23, 2018 judgment in the same case it permitted the manufacture and sale of improved and green crackers, subject to conditions.The framework tightened again. In its April 3, 2025 order in the Arjun Gopal matter, the court recorded a complete ban in Delhi-NCR on the manufacture, storage, sale and use of firecrackers, citing the region's pollution situation. It added that any relaxation would depend on scientific evidence that green crackers caused the "bare minimum" pollution.In October 2025, the court eased this for Diwali. Its October 15, 2025 order allowed the sale of green crackers listed on the CSIR-NEERI website from October 18 to 20, only through licensed traders at designated locations. Crackers brought in from outside NCR were restricted.Barium-based and unapproved products were prohibited, laris and serial crackers were barred, and so was online sale and purchase.This year follows the same broad template. The November 2, 2026 directions allow certified green crackers on November 7 and 8, between 6am and 7am and between 8pm and 10pm. Bursting is prohibited within 300 metres of hospitals, nursing homes, health centres, old-age homes and notified silence zones. The complete ban is restored from November 9.A practice once governed mainly by custom now runs on court orders, designated markets, product restrictions and compliance deadlines.Why Delhi's AQI is not Noida'sDelhi-NCR celebrates on the same dates, but it is not governed as one city.Delhi, Noida, Ghaziabad, Gurugram and Faridabad come under different municipal bodies, state governments and pollution-control authorities. Enforcement, market regulation, sanitation and environmental monitoring therefore involve different administrations and agencies.That matters for any comparison. A reading from Delhi cannot automatically stand in for Noida, Gurugram, Ghaziabad or Faridabad. The Central Pollution Control Board's AQI bulletin for October 30, 2016, for instance, recorded Delhi at 431, Faridabad at 410 and Gurugram at 317 at 4pm. Those were three separate readings, not one regional average.The same applies to 2025 and 2026. Each city needs its own official reading, and the restrictions for each jurisdiction have to be checked separately.What Diwali's air tells us, and what it doesn'tAir quality is one part of the changing Diwali record, but it is not the whole story.On October 30, 2016, the CPCB's 4pm bulletin put Delhi's AQI at 431, in the "severe" category. On Diwali 2025, October 20, the AQI stood at 345 at 4pm, in the "very poor" category, according to CPCB data.That is 86 points lower. But Diwali fell 10 days earlier on the calendar in 2025, and an earlier festival meets different temperatures, winds, humidity and stubble-burning conditions. The gap is an indicator. It is not proof that restrictions alone produced cleaner air.The CPCB's report on air quality during Deepawali 2016 recorded very high particulate matter at individual stations. At Pitampura, PM10 stood at 1,297 micrograms per cubic metre and PM2.5 at 1,238. At ITO, the readings were 878 and 797. These are station-level readings, not citywide averages, and they cannot be compared directly with an AQI.The same report noted a mean wind speed of 1.3 metres per second on Diwali 2016, against 3.4 metres per second in 2015. The Diwali-night mixing height was 152 metres, compared with 324 metres the year before.These numbers show why air monitoring has become part of the festival's official record. They do not, on their own, establish how much of the pollution came from firecrackers, or how conditions varied across the NCR.What the record can't tell usThe official record captures some of the biggest shifts around Diwali: the rise of digital payments, the evolving regulatory framework and the growing role of environmental monitoring.It does not tell us whether households celebrate differently, whether neighbourhood markets have lost ground to online platforms, or why the air in 2025 was better than in 2016. Answering those would need comparable commercial, mobility and enforcement data that no single bulletin provides.What the record does show is that the machinery around the festival looks very different from 2016. This Diwali, the lamps may be much the same. articles.title: Aramco China Championship: Mimi Rhodes and fellow English players miss out on title as Spain's Ana Pelaez storms to victory
articles.summary: Spain's Ana Pelaez records seven birdies and a hole-in-one as she wins Ladies European Tour title in Shenzhen; England's Mimi Rhodes finishes outright second, three shots adrift, with compatriots Charlotte Heath and Annabell Fuller sealing top-10 places; Shuri Sakuma triumphs on LPGA Tour
articles.body:
Heath shared the lead with Pelaez's compatriot Luna Sobron on 16 under after round three in Shenzhen, with Rhodes one shot back and Fuller three strokes adrift.

Fuller stared superbly on Sunday with four birdies in her first six holes lifting her to 16 under but she then registered three bogeys on her back nine ahead of a closing birdie to end up on 14 under and in ninth spot after a one-under day, six shots behind Pelaez.

With Heath only able to card an even-par 73, mixing two birdies with as many bogeys, Rhodes, a three-time winner on the Ladies European Tour in 2025, was the highest-placed of the English contingent, finishing in outright second on 17 under.

The 24-year-old, who made her Solheim Cup debut in September as Team Europe defeated Team USA in the Netherlands, registered birdies at four and 17 as she signed for a blemish-free, two-under 71.

Pelaez was irresistible on the day, with her round-of-the-week 64 at Mission Hills featuring seven birdies, including three in a row to finish, and an ace at the par-three 13th as claimed her first victory on the tour since the 2022 Madrid Ladies Open.

Pelaez's fellow Spaniard Sobron finished in a share of third place on 16 under after an even-par 73, alongside Heath and China's Shiyuan Zhou, Ruixin Liu and Liqi Zeng.

Another Englishwoman, Alice Hewson, came 20th on 11 under.

Peleaz: Most enjoyable round I have ever played

Pelaez, who began the final round in 10th place, five shots off the lead, said: "It's been tough. At one point, I thought I would never be in this position again. It's hard to believe in yourself when you're not feeling okay.

"Coming back, playing golf and enjoying it is just a gift. If we can add on winning or top 10 then good, if not, it's okay. It's for life itself. You might have good moments or moments that are uncomfortable, but you have got to keep going.

"I know deep in my heart that it was the most enjoyable round I have ever played. I think it's because hard work does pay off. I have been trying to win, but not needing to win as enjoying the game was the most important [thing]."

The Ladies European Tour now has a two-week break before the season-ending Andalucía Costa del Sol Open de España from November 26-29, a tournament you can watch live on Sky Sports.

On the LPGA Tour, Shuri Sakuma won her first title on the circuit with a four-shot victory at the Toto Japan Classic in her homeland.

Sakuma, who had won eight times previously on the LPGA of Japan Tour, carded an eight-under closing round of 64 to reach 20 under for the tournament, with 54-hole leader Akie Iwai finishing second on 16 under after a one-under 71 at Taihelyo Club Minori Course.

The Toto Japan Classic was the final part of the LPGA Tour's late-season 'Asian Swing', after the Buick LPGA Shanghai in China, BMW Ladies Championship in South Korea and Maybank Championship in Malaysia.

The tour returns to the USA next week for The Annika in Florida, live on Sky Sports Golf and Sky Sports Main Event from 4pm on Thursday.

Sweden's Linn Grant won the event in 2025 after Nelly Korda had done so in three of the previous four seasons.

articles.title: Ana Peláez gana el Aramco de China con una soberbia remontada y un hoyo en uno
articles.standfirst: La malagueña tira 64 golpes y enjuga los cinco de desventaja con los que había llegado a la última ronda
articles.summary: La malagueña tira 64 golpes y enjuga los cinco de desventaja con los que había llegado a la última ronda
articles.body: Ana Peláez se llevó el triunfo`en el Aramco China Championship de una manera que no se olvida. La malagueña de 28 años protagonizó una remontada de época, cinco golpes, para conquistar su segundo torneo en el Ladies European Tour tras el Open de Madrid que levantó en 2022. La última hora y media del torneo fue soñada. Empezó con un hoyo en uno en el par 3 del hoyo 13 y se completó con tres birdies en los tres últimos tramos para batir por tres golpes a la inglesa Mimi Rhodes, una jugadora que participó en la victoria de Europa en septiembre en Paises Bajos en la Solheim Cup. Una inglesa casi andaluza. Aprendió a jugar en La Cañada y ahora pertenece a la escudería de La Reserva de Sotogrande. Pelaéz, de Finca Cortesín, firmó 64 golpes en un recorrido de par 73. Colosal. (Resultados) Peláez firmó la mejor tarjeta del domingo y, de largo, la mejor de todas las que estaban arriba, entre ellas Luna Sobrón, que había alcanzado el último día como líder y que alternó birdies y bogey el domingo. Seis errores, dos en los primeros pares 5, y otros tantos aciertos le condenaron a la tercera plaza como a Charlotte Heath, ganadora este año en La Sella. La golfista española recibe así recompensa a varias temporadas de lucha. Tras una buena carrera amateur, encontró pronto en éxito en el profesionalismo e intentó la aventura americana sin éxito. Ahora, tras varios cambios, en busca de entrenamientos inteligentes, da con su segunda victoria en un escenario tan simbólico como Mission HIlls. “Ha sido duro, pero ahora me siento bien. Hubo un momento en que pensé que nunca volvería a estar en esta posición. Es difícil creer en uno mismo cuando no te encuentras bien”, declaró la ganadora. “Volver a jugar al golf y disfrutarlo es un verdadero regalo. Si podemos ganar o quedar entre los diez primeros, mejor; si no, no pasa nada. Es parte de la vida misma. Puede que tengas buenos momentos o momentos incómodos, pero tienes que seguir adelante".

articles.title: Jon Rahm gana en Abu Dhabi y es el rey de las Rolex Series
articles.standfirst: El de Barrika suma seis de los torneos elevados y conquista su primer éxito tras salir del LIV Golf
articles.summary: El de Barrika suma seis de los torneos elevados y conquista su primer éxito tras salir del LIV Golf
articles.body: Una versión muy alta de Jon Rahm se alzó con la victoria en el Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, su primera victoria desde que se desligó del LIV Golf, el circuito que ha gobernado durante tres años. Es la undécima victoria en el DP World Tour, la liga en la que no ganaba desde el Masters de Augusta 2023. Es su sexta victoria en los Rolex Series, los Masters 1.000 del golf europeo para los neófitos. Es su tercer título de 2026, el primero, además, desde que fue padre por cuarta vez. (Resultados) Durante un domingo de poco viento, banderas exigentes y sol, Jon se vio achuchado por varios. Especialmente por Rory McIlroy, el jugador que encarnaba la tradición -pantalón largo- y que persigue su octava Orden de Mérito e igualar así a Colin Montgomerie. Eugenio López-Chacarra, que acabó vigésimo segundo y sigue liderando, se lo va a poner difícil la próxima semana. También Tyrrell Hatton y el italiano Francesco Laporta no perdían el rastro alcanzada, tras el hoyo 11, la veintena de golpes bajo par en grupo. Entonces, metió Jon el último cambio de ritmo. Puede que en mes y medio haya vivido más pendiente de llevar a sus hijos a la guarderia y otras tareas que de afinar los palos, pero cuando coge calle juega unos hierros fabulosos. De ser preciso desde el tee se ha asegurado él y su caddie Adam Hayes esta semana. Un recorrido sin árboles, aunque sí con una hierba alta exigente, puede invitar a soltar el driver a todo trapo, pero Jon fue inteligente. Jugó muchas veces la madera, obligándose a golpes más largos, pero que los movió luego de maravilla. Enlazó birdies en el 11 (par 5) y en el 12 y abrió una diferencia de dos con los tres perseguidores. Sólo habia cometido un bogey antes, en el hoyo 3 y porque cayó en un bunker de calle. Se le habían escapado los dos primeros tramos largos, pero por fin acertó con el tercero. Fue un impulso definitivo para un jugador que no mostró fisuras. Los últimos seis hoyos exigían arriesgar a Laporta, McIlroy y Hatton. Al primero, el número 224 del ránking mundial, le pesó la altura del combate. Un triple bogey en el 13 (par 3) lo descartó. Rory, con una uña del pie izquierdo molestándolo, no acertaba en los greenes. En el 15, un bogey lo relegó a 19 bajo par y con sólo tres hoyos por delante, quedaba también descartado. El pulso era entre Rahm y Hatton, los dos amigos, ex compañeros en la Legión XIII, compañeros de tragos cuando hubo que celebrar cosas, como el año pasado cuando coincidió el segundo título de Jon en el LIV con la clasificación matemática para la Ryder Cup del incandescente inglés. Los dos únicos golfistas con cinco Rolex Series en el palmarés. Jon no esperó mucho para el siguiente empujón. Otro hierro fantástico a un metro del agujero en el 15 elevó su tanteo a 23 bajo par, aunque la respuesta de Hatton fue la misma. El vasco seguia cogiendo calles (12 de 14 hizo) y eso le sirvió de garantía hasta el final. Terminó con 67 golpes y ganando por dos. Alzó los brazos, en fin, por vigésimo quinta vez en su carrera profesional. Tras tres años dominando el LIV Golf, un circuito que demasiada crítica lo observó siempre con recelo, necesitaba un golpe de autoridad inmediato para acreditar que su status está entre los tres mejores del planeta. Está por ver si llegará a un acuerdo con el PGA Tour y que el golf recupere las grandes batallas de antaño con Scheffler y compañía. De momento, volverá el lunes al top 10 mundial. El festival español se completó con Ángel Ayora y David Puig. El de San Roque, 22 años, fue quinto a pesar de un triple bogey y un doble bogey durante la semana. Tiró 67 golpes el domingo. Ha hecho birdie a todos los hoyos del campo menos al 15 en la suma de las cuatro vueltas. Sus aspiraciones a ganarse uno de los 10 billetes del PGA Tour -a los que se postulan también Nacho Elvira y Ángel Hidalgo- aumentan. Puig, que también podría alcanzar ese propósito, acabó a su lado con un trabajado 70.

articles.title: Abu Dhabi Championship: Jon Rahm beats Tyrrell Hatton, Rory McIlroy to Rolex Series win and boosts Race to Dubai hopes
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy moved above Patrick Reed to second in the Race to Dubai standings; McIlroy finished four strokes behind Jon Rahm, who claimed a two-shot win over Tyrrell Hatton on his Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship debut
articles.body:
Rahm mixed six birdies with a lone bogey during a five-under 67 at Yas Links GC, lifting him to 23 under on his tournament debut and closing out a record sixth Rolex Series victory.

The Spaniard took a one-shot lead into the final day at Yas Links GC and briefly lost his overnight advantage with Hatton, McIlroy and Francesco Laporta all leading at various points during an eventful Sunday.

Hatton finished second ahead of McIlroy, who made a birdie-eagle start to his final round before finishing four strokes back in third - his 11th top-three finish in 15 starts in Abu Dhabi, with Laporta ending in fourth spot on 17 under.

McIlroy moved above Patrick Reed into second and became Eugenio Chacarra's closest challenger in the season-long standings, while Rahm's victory - his first since departing LIV Golf - keeps him in contention to win the Race to Dubai.

How Rahm beat Ryder Cup team-mates to victory

McIlroy - playing in the penultimate group - made the dream start to his final round when he drove the green at the 378-yard par-four first and two-putted for birdie, then holed a putt from nearly 50 feet to eagle the par-five second.

The Northern Irishman dropped a shot at the par-four third, where Rahm undid his opening-hole birdie by finding two fairway bunkers and making bogey, as Laporta pulled ahead after posting two birdies in his first three holes.

Rahm set up a close-range birdie at the fifth and holed from 25 feet to add another at the next, as Hatton also made back-to-back gains, only for Laporta to take advantage of the par-five seventh and pull level with the Spaniard.

McIlroy cancelled out a bogey at the sixth by birdieing the next but was still two behind until he started his back nine with successive birdies, making it a three-way tie at the top.

Rahm and Laporta edged back ahead with two-putt birdies at the par-five 11th, before a two-shot swing next saw Rahm convert from close range as his playing partner made bogey.

Laporta's title challenge ended with a triple-bogey at the par-three 13th, while McIlroy experienced a cold putter on the back nine and saw his hopes dashed when he missed from five feet to save par at the 15th.

Rahm tidied up from four feet to match the birdie of Hatton at the 15th, keeping him two ahead of the Englishman with three to play, with pars over the closing three holes enough to complete a first DP World Tour win since before he joined LIV Golf.

"It's been quite a while since I've played good in a DP World Tour event!" Rahm admitted. "As far as I'm concerned, except the shot on 17, I played a pretty flawless back nine.

"After everything that's gone on, and some poor play, and some battles mentally, with a lot of noise, to come back out [and win] after a little bit of rest after having a new baby, it's quite special."

McIlroy rues missed chances but boosts Race to Dubai hopes

Race to Dubai leader Chacarra ended tied-22nd and Patrick Reed finished tied-43rd, allowing McIlroy to move within 533.93 points of No 1 spot and maintain his push for a record-equalling eighth Order of Merit title.

"It was a week where I felt like I had my chances," McIlroy said. "Especially today, birdieing 10 and 11 on the back to get tied for the lead, then I had two good chances on 12 and 13 and didn't make those. Had to scramble for par on 14 and then I just couldn't keep my momentum going.

"It was a good week. I saw some encouraging signs in the game. I'm going to be in that final group going out on Thursday. I obviously would have loved to have won the tournament, but enough positive signs to feel good about going into next week."

On the challenge of holding off McIlroy, Chacarra said: "It [Race to Dubai] is hard. He's the No 2 player in the world and the No 1 in Europe and he's been doing it for a long time. Obviously the odds are on him and he's the favourite, but we'll play golf.

"We know what I'm capable of when I am playing good. There was a lot of good this week, but I just need to sharpen the bat to have a chance next week."

The DP World Tour season reaches its climax next week at the DP World Tour Championship, where only the top 50 available players in the Race to Dubai standings are eligible to compete.

articles.title: Abu Dhabi Championship: Jon Rahm pips Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy to win on DP World Tour
articles.summary: Jon Rahm fires a final-round 67 to clinch a two-shot victory ahead of Tyrrell Hatton at the Abu Dhabi Championship.
articles.body:
Abu Dhabi Championship final-round leaderboard

23 J Rahm (Spa); - 21 T Hatton (Eng); -19 R McIlroy (NI); -17 F Laporta (Ita); -16 B Wiesberger (Aut), A Ayora (Spa), D Puig (Spa); -15 J Schaper (SA)

Selected others: -14 N Kimsey (Eng), M Jordan (Eng); -13 S Bairstow (Eng), T Fleetwood (Eng), A Sullivan (Eng); -12 E Ferguson (Sco); -11 E Chacarra (Spa); -10 A Rai (Eng); -9 M Wallace (Eng); -4 P Reed (US)

Jon Rahm fired a final-round 67 to clinch a two-shot victory over England's Tyrrell Hatton at the Abu Dhabi Championship.

It was a first victory for the two-time major winner since he announced his departure from LIV Golf, and a first win at a DP World Tour event in four years.

The Spaniard, in his first tournament since the birth of his fourth child last month, produced six birdies with just one dropped shot on Sunday to finish clear of Hatton with Northern Ireland's Rory McIlroy another two strokes further back.

"It means a lot. It's been quite a while to play well in the DP World Tour," Rahm told Sky Sports.

"Except a shot on 17, as far as I'm concerned, I played a pretty flawless back nine. It was really solid, never in danger of making a bogey except that one hole.

"After everything that has gone on, some poor play and some battles mentally with a lot of noise, to come back out after a bit of a break and a new addition to the family, it's pretty special."

Having finished at the very bottom of the leaderboard at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth in his last appearance, Rahm joked that going "last to first" was especially pleasing.

For McIlroy, his third-placed finish was enough to ensure he goes into next week's season-finale at the DP World Tour Championship sitting second in the Race To Dubai standings as he seeks a record-equalling eighth win.

The 37-year-old, who was given a two-shot penalty in his first round, leapfrogged American Patrick Reed and now trails only Spain's Eugenio Chacarra in his bid to match Colin Montgomerie's eight season-long titles.

Despite starting the week outside the top 50, Rahm's victory ensured he remained in the hunt too should he be able to go back-to-back in Dubai.

Rahm was not 'willing to follow' LIV 2.0 path

Rahm sacrifices £75m to secure exit from LIV Golf

Rahm had taken an overnight lead of a single stroke into Sunday after a third-round 66.

His Ryder Cup team-mates Hatton and McIlroy, as well as Italian Francesco Laporta, managed to carry the chase into the back nine on Sunday.

Laporta, chasing a maiden DP World Tour success, produced three birdies on the front nine to make the turn in a tie with playing partner Rahm.

McIlroy, in the group further ahead, picked up a pair of shots on the 11th and 12th to join them on 20 under.

Across the closing stretch, however, Rahm's challengers fell away.

After he matched McIlroy's birdie at the par-five 12th, the six-time major winner missed a birdie putt on the 13th before dropping a shot on the 15th thanks to a wayward approach.

He would finish with a three-under 69 on the day to seal his 11th top-three finish at a tournament he still has yet to win.

Having left the 11th green four under for his day, Laporta dropped four shots in two holes to tumble out of contention.

The 36-year-old, who led after the second round, finished in fourth, six shots off the pace.

Hatton, whose final-round 68 included four birdies and 14 pars, briefly closed the gap to a single shot on the 15th, but Rahm matched the Englishman's birdie moments later with a three-foot putt following a brilliant six iron on to the green.

While there was a further chance to increase the pressure on the leader heading to the final hole, Hatton's 24-foot birdie putt came up inches short on the 17th, before Rahm's par putt dropped from under five feet.

Race To Dubai leader Chacarra finished on 11 under in a three-way tie for 22nd, while Reed ended on four under.

articles.title: Race to Dubai: Rory McIlroy takes 'positive signs' into DP World Tour Championship after missing out on Abu Dhabi win
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy moved above Patrick Reed to second in the Race to Dubai standings; McIlroy ended third at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, four strokes behind Ryder Cup team-mate Jon Rahm; watch the DP World Tour Championship live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
McIlroy made a birdie-eagle start to his final round at Yas Links GC and held a share of the lead again with seven holes remaining, only to finish in third spot, four strokes behind Ryder Cup team-mate Jon Rahm .

He played the last seven holes of his three-under 69 in one over, seeing him end the week on 19 under, leaving McIlroy without a worldwide victory since successfully defending his title at The Masters in April.

"It was sort of a week where I felt like I had my chances," McIlroy admitted. "Especially today, birdieing 10 and 11 on the back nine to get tied for the lead. Then I had two good chances, 12 and 13, and didn't make those.

"Had to scramble for par on 14 and then I just couldn't keep my momentum going, but it was a good week. I saw some encouraging signs in the game."

McIlroy's third-place finish represents the 11th time he has come in the top three in 15 appearances in Abu Dhabi without victory, with the result lifting him above Patrick Reed into second in the Race to Dubai standings heading into the season finale.

The world No 2 now trails Eugenio Chacarra by 533.93 points going into the DP World Tour Championship, where 2,000 points are on offer for the winner and 1,335 points for second, with McIlroy challenging for a record-equalling eighth Order of Merit.

"I'm going to be in that final group going out on Thursday," McIlroy added. "I obviously would have loved to have won the tournament, but enough positive signs to feel good about going into next week.

"That [final group] is where I wanted to be. It's a pretty familiar spot for me going into the DP World Tour Championship, and I'm excited for it.

"That was the goal coming into these two weeks, to try to catch Eugenio [Chacarra] and Patrick [Reed] and try to win the Race to Dubai again.

"It would have been great to win this week and give myself not as much of a deficit, or even a lead, but still feel like I'm right in there with a great chance."

McIlroy set for Chacarra showdown in Dubai

Chacarra has topped the standings since winning the DP World India Championship in October, his third victory of the season, with the Spaniard looking to find improvements in his game after failing to contend in Abu Dhabi.

"Drove the ball amazing the last two days and still made so many mistakes," Chacarra admitted. "A lot of little mistakes that got me out of being up there.

"My good was really good. I got a lot of birdies and hit really good long shots and made some good putts, but obviously I need to sharpen my short game and my wedges. It's a little frustrating because it's something we've been working on.

"Obviously the odds are on him [McIlroy] and he's the favourite, but we'll play golf. We know what I'm capable of when I am playing good. There was a lot of good this week, but I just need to sharpen the bat to have a chance next week."

Nine players still have a mathematical chance of winning the Race to Dubai, with Rahm now among those after an 11th DP World Tour title - his first since The Masters in 2023 and a record-breaking sixth Rolex Series victory.

"I didn't think I would ever have a chance to win it," admitted Rahm, who jumped to sixth in the standings. "Actually gives me a little extra incentive next week. Those are better odds than I expected so looking forward to it and hopefully I can get my fourth one [DP World Tour Championship]."

The DP World Tour season reaches its climax next week at the DP World Tour Championship, where only the top 50 available players in the Race to Dubai standings are eligible to compete.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy defends Scottie Scheffler amid lazy criticisms about World No 1's non-global schedule
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy defends Scottie Scheffler against critics who say the world No. 1 should travel more, calling it his prerogative as a family man.
articles.body: Scottie Scheffler is the best golfer on Earth and has been recognized as such for 176 consecutive weeks. Being the No. 1-ranked player in the world for more than three years running comes with a spotlight, and with a spotlight comes criticism. What makes Scheffler different than most who have ever been in his position is that he doesn't care about the spotlight, not even a little bit. Scheffler boasts about the fact that golf does not define him and that the game falls well below both his faith and young family on the list of most important things in his life. If you were to ask either a golf fan or even his peers to describe Scheffler, most would say he's a very normal person who loves spending time with his family, who also happens to be a generational talent with a golf club in his hand. These circumstances, coupled with his style of play where he'll ball-strike his opponents to death, have led to his biggest criticism being that he is simply 'boring.' In recent months, however, some of the criticism's focus has turned to his playing schedule. SCOTTIE SCHEFFLER SHARES A PERFECTLY IMPERFECT ASSESSMENT OF WORK-LIFE BALANCE, THE CHALLENGES OF FATHERHOOD In September, Golf Monthly published a column claiming that Scheffler has an obligation to travel the world and be a "global ambassador" for the game as the world No. 1. "One thing he absolutely should be criticised for, though, is the fact he’s seemingly allergic to leaving America for more than a fortnight each year," the column stated, after noting that he is not trying to be someone he isn't. The 30-year-old made 20 starts during the 2026 PGA Tour season, with just the Scottish Open and Open Championship taking place outside of the United States. He won three times, earning just shy of $31 million. The timing of the story coming in the fall, with Scheffler already in the midst of his "offseason," led to a discussion about whether or not he did have a responsibility to play all around the world, and it has continued all the way into November. RORY MCILROY FIRES BACK AT KEVIN KISNER AFTER 'DOGS---' COMMENT ABOUT GROWING THE GAME The topic has even reached Rory McIlroy's orbit, and the six-time major champion believes anyone saying Scheffler needs to travel the world more is wrong. "People have their own decisions to make and their own lives, and I’ve seen criticism of Scottie Scheffler because Scottie doesn’t play — but that’s his decision," McIlroy said ahead of this week's Abu Dhabi Aldar Golf Championship. "If he doesn’t want to, that’s his prerogative. I think Scottie being Scottie is good enough for the world of golf, and he doesn’t need to travel all over the world because he’s got a young family, and that doesn’t bring value to his life; where I like travel, it’s all I’ve known." CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE It's straightforward, which is extremely rare in today's world, but Scheffler shouldn't be criticized for not wanting to travel the world to play a game, simply because he's the best at that game. Scheffler has earned the right to control every single aspect of his schedule as the No. 1-ranked player in the world for three years running. Those on the other side of the argument would also have to side with the idea that the PGA Tour calendar isn't good enough, which is objectively ridiculous. Scheffler is an American who enjoys playing, and winning, in America and prioritizes sleeping in his own home under the same roof as his family as much as he possibly can. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER To criticize any athlete for that, let alone the best on planet Earth at their respective sport, is just a poor attempt at making something out of nothing.

articles.title: Chevron's winner's jump gets permanent home as Memorial Park pond is completed
articles.summary: Memorial Park added a pond to the 18th hole to preserve the LPGA tradition of winners jumping into the water.
articles.body:
The new pond along the right side of Memorial Park's 18th hole is complete.

The site of the LPGA's Chevron Championship , the first women's major of the year, as well as rhe PGA Tour's Texas Children's Houston Open, will have a new hazard for players to deal with coming down the stretch in 2027 and beyond.

Architect Tom Doak returned to help re-design the closing hole at the municipal facility about 5 miles west of downtown Houston, adding a pond that flanks the right side of the green on the closing par 4.

The Astros Golf Foundation helped fund a $34 million renovation of the course, and the PGA Tour returned to the facility in the fall of 2020. Last year, the LPGA moved the Chevron to Memorial Park after three years in The Woodlands, a northern suburb of Houston.

Why the change? The LPGA and tradition is why.

Amy Alcott started the tradition of the Chevron winner jumping into Poppie's Pond back in 1988 at Mission Hills. That tradition continued at The Club at Carlton Woods for three years, but there was no water feature on the 18th hole at Memorial Park.

Last year, after the conclusion of the Houston Open, crews constructed a temporary pool, which measured 15 feet by 10 feet and 4 1/2 feet deep and cost roughly $60,000, for the winner to jump into and continue the tradition. Nelly Korda won her second Chevron title and celebrated with the customary jump, doing a cannonball.

"If I'm hoisting the trophy then I'm jumping in," Korda said after her win. "I'm going to keep the tradition alive. Everyone is going to have their own opinion. My opinion is if you kill a tradition it's going to be gone forever. They're making the effort to wanting to continue the legacy of the jump, and there is a lot of the effort from Chevron, from Glenn (Weckerlin), Mike Wirth, to wanting this tradition to move on, and, you know, yeah."

The change drastically changes the shape of the 18th green. The front right portion of the formerly large putting surface is now gone, with the pond lurking for any approach shots that leak right. There's a narrow entry on the left side of the green, and the surface gets larger for any shots that are hit toward the back. Two bunkers await shots that go too far left at the front of the green, so accuracy will be paramount for players starting in 2027.

There's now water in play on the final four holes at Memorial Park, making it an even tougher closing stretch for players trying to hoist a major trophy. And for those who conquer the stretch, they'll have a nice pond to cool off in with a celebratory leap starting in 2027.

Cameron Jourdan is an assistant editor of Golfweek, covering college and amateur golf, the PGA Tour and plenty more. Follow Cameron on X/Twitter (@Cam_Jourdan) or Instagram (@GolfweekJourdan).

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau Addresses LIV Decision and Future, Reveals Next Golf Tournament on His Schedule
articles.summary: After LIV Golf shuttered its league last week, Bryson DeChambeau released a lengthy statement on Sunday addressing his future.
articles.body:
After LIV Golf shuttered its league last week, Bryson DeChambeau released a lengthy statement on Sunday addressing his future.

DeChambeau said he doesn't regret leaving the PGA Tour to join the now-defunct breakaway league, and he plans to return to action next month.

"Whatever comes next, I'll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before me," he stated. "In December, I'll compete at the Nedbank Golf Challenge, Gary Player's event, in front of fans who made my first visit to South Africa unforgettable. Beyond that, I'll go about whatever is next the right way."

Per ESPN's Mark Schlabach and Paolo Uggetti , a LIV Golf attorney told a U.S. Bankruptcy Court judge that the league would file a new Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan after failing to secure the necessary financial commitment and player support to proceed with LIV 2.0.

"The debtors were ultimately unable to bring the key parties to a fully consensual arrangement that would have supported a financially viable LIV 2.0 league," attorney Matthew Williams said during the hearing. "As a result, the debtors are not currently proceeding with the LIV 2.0 plan. Instead, the debtors are toggling to a value-maximizing wind-down of their business."

DeChambeau joined LIV Golf in 2022 and quickly became one of the faces of the league. He admitted in his statement on Sunday that he may have made some mistakes during his tenure.

"I still believe in team golf. It may look different in the future, but I still believe it's essential to growing the game. Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that, along the way, I've said some things that didn't help," he stated.

Rex Hoggard of the Golf Channel recently reported that DeChambeau will not have an easy path back to the PGA Tour, so it remains to be seen if the two-time U.S. Open champion will be able to restore his reputation in the sport.

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau issues statement on LIV Golf after league scraps reboot plans and files for bankruptcy
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau issues statement on LIV Golf after league scraps reboot plans and files for bankruptcy: DeChambeau has lost his DP World Tour exemption for 2028 and 2029.
articles.body:
LIV Golf has confirmed plans to wind down operations and enter liquidation, abandoning hopes of launching a new version due to a lack of financial backing. Lawyers representing the company confirmed the plans during a bankruptcy hearing in New Jersey on Thursday.

DeChambeau has until November 15 to declare his intention to become a DP World Tour member in 2027, or risk being frozen out of professional golf. He has defended his decision to join LIV from the outset and thanked his supporters in a statement posted on X on Sunday.

"I'm not going to rewrite the last four years," DeChambeau wrote.

"I made a decision I believed in, and I'm grateful for what came with it: playing in front of fans new and old around the world who rarely got to see the best players at home. The record crowds in Adelaide and Johannesburg will stick with me for the rest of my life.

"I believed this game could reach more people, in more places, in a new way. I still believe that. And I gave it everything I had to keep team golf alive.

"I want to say thank you to the people who believed in this from the start: the staff, the operations crews, the caddies, and everyone behind the scenes at LIV and Crushers GC who bet their careers on this. You gave everything. And thank you to my Crushers team-mates, our sponsors, and every fan who came out.

"I still believe in team golf. It may look different in the future, but I still believe it's essential to growing the game."

The two-time major champion explained last week that he was hopeful the league could "exist forever" , with Dechambeau also revealing he had played a role in plotting out how LIV 2.0 could move forward.

Despite LIV's impending liquidation, the American golfer remained tight-lipped about his own future:

"Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that, along the way, I've said some things that didn't help. Whatever comes next, I'll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before me.

"In December, I'll compete at the Nedbank Golf Challenge, Gary Player's event, in front of fans who made my first visit to South Africa unforgettable. Beyond that, I'll go about whatever is next the right way.

"My passion has been to grow this game. That's still the goal. Thank you for sticking with me.

"Together we can all grow this great game we love."

Analysis by Sky Sports News' Jamie Weir:

Love him or hate him, DeChambeau has star factor. He puts bums on seats, he commands eyeballs and column inches. He is box office.

Until the bitter end, he believed fully in LIV 2.0, the phoenix from the flames version of the beleaguered and controversial golf tour.

One source told me that in a meeting of LIV's 13 team captains in August, when the end was seemingly nigh, DeChambeau was the only one who still passionately felt there was a way forward and attempted to win over the other 12, who were resigned to LIV's fate. No one was willing to take that leap into the unknown with him.

By virtue of winning the 2024 US Open at Pinehurst, DeChambeau earned a five-year exemption on the DP World Tour. However, the rules state that for every year a major champion fails to take up his membership, they lose a year off the end of this period.

In other words, having failed to take up DP World Tour membership in 2025 and 2026, DeChambeau lost his exemption for 2028 and 2029.

That means he does still have the option of taking up membership for the 2027 season, but must inform the tour of his intention to do so by its deadline of November 15.

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau reflects on his LIV Golf days without revealing future plans: 'Gave it everything I had'
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau is closing the door on his LIV Golf days.
articles.body:
Days after LIV Golf effectively ceased operations , Bryson DeChambeau, its most ardent defender, has spoken up about his own journey through four years with the breakaway tour.

"I made a decision I believed in," DeChambeau said in a statement released to social media on Sunday morning, "and I'm grateful for what came with it."

DeChambeau, who won the 2024 U.S. Open as captain of LIV's Crushers GC team, ascended from quirky talent to worldwide star while playing for LIV. However, that was largely a result of his non-LIV exploits — his massively popular YouTube channel, his ongoing narratives with other golf influencers, and his never-dull majors performances. While playing in golf's greatest tournaments, DeChambeau did everything from defeat Rory McIlroy head-to-head in Pinehurst in 2024 to embroil himself in a spectacular rules controversy at this season's Open Championship at Royal Birkdale.

DeChambeau is a thrilling, infuriating and always watchable player, which made him one of LIV's most notable assets. He preached the gospel of team golf right up to Sunday's statement: "I still believe in team golf. It may look different in the future, but I still believe it's essential to growing the game."

He also seemed to concede that his public image has broken containment.

"Arnold Palmer always said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that," DeChambeau said. "I've said some things that didn't help. Whatever comes next, I'll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before me."

That would seem to be an "acknowledgement" that he's going to have to accept responsibility for past actions — which include filing suit against the PGA Tour in LIV's earliest days — before he'll be allowed back onto the world's marquee tour … if he is at all.

DeChambeau's next move is a mystery. He could opt to follow fellow LIV star Jon Rahm to the DP World Tour for a year. The league has reportedly offered him full status in 2027, but he has until Nov. 15 to opt in.

He could opt to play only in the majors — he's exempted into all through 2029, and the U.S. Open through 2034 — and play YouTube golf . He could attempt to beseech his way back onto the PGA Tour the way Brooks Koepka did, although that pathway appears extremely unlikely. He's next slated to tee up at the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa next month, an event that is hosted by Gary Player and co-sanctioned byt the DP World Tour.

No matter what he chooses, DeChambeau will have a significant role in golf going forward. He's too large of a personality — and too large of a talent — to stay in the background for long.

articles.title: 5 takeaways from Lions’ 19-9 win against Dolphins
articles.summary: 5 takeaways from the Detroit Lions’ win against the Miami Dolphins, 19-9.
articles.body:
Entering Week 9 on a three-game winning streak, the Detroit Lions flew down south to face the Miami Dolphins. The Lions offense was expected to have a big game, but was held to just 19 points against a Dolphins defense that gave them fits. Those 19 points were enough in the end as Detroit's defense held Miami to just nine points.

Here are my five takeaways from the Lions' victory against the Dolphins.

Miles Frazier gets his first career start

The biggest storyline was left guard Christian Mahogany not getting the start. He did play on special teams, so it wasn't an injury. The CBS broadcast said the reason was a "coaching decision." With him not getting the start, the team called on backup guard Miles Frazier to play left guard.

After the game, Lions head coach Dan Campbell was asked about this and explained why Frazier got the start.

"That was team rules (for) Mahogany. It was really that simple," Campbell said. "Miles deserved his opportunity, so he got it. Doesn't mean it stays that way, but that was the way it was going to be today."

Hopefully Mahogany can get back on the team's good side, or else he could cost himself not just a job, but a possible contract extension in the future.

Detroit's offensive line struggled against a struggling Miami defense. Frazier was a big part of the problem, missing blocks repeatedly and struggling to hold his blocks, but he wasn't the only culprit. Right tackle Blake Miller had his worst game of the season, allowing tons of pressure and looking like a rookie.

Lions quarterback Jared Goff was sacked three times, and he threw his second interception of the season when Dolphins EDGE Josh Uche hit him as he threw. Goff was also hit as he threw another pass that was initially ruled a fumble recovered by the Dolphins for a touchdown, but it was overturned to an incomplete pass. Goff faced pressure for most of the game, and it hurt the offense.

In the running game, running back Jahmyr Gibbs was limited in his lanes, rushing 20 times for 74 yards and was the only player to find the end zone. We have seen what this team looks like when the offensive line struggles—look back at the 2025 season. Hopefully Mahogany and backup center Cade Mays can return for the trip to Germany next week, as performances like this won't win you many games.

The calls for firing Kelvin Sheppard have quieted down

After a long September where the Lions' defense was a liability, it has become an asset in their last four games. They allowed 21 points against the Arizona Cardinals, but held the Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, and Miami Dolphins to 16, 15, and nine points respectively. This defense is creating turnovers, generating pressure, and stopping the running game.

Remember when fans were clamoring for Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard to be fired? This team was also without starting EDGE DJ Wonnum, cornerback D.J. Reed, and linebacker Jack Campbell. The good news is Wonnum and Reed should be back soon, and safety Kerby Joseph is getting closer to returning. With the play improving and players returning from injury soon, this defense is starting to turn a corner.

Down multiple starters, the defense performed well overall, holding Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II to 55 yards, just 3.4 yards per carry. Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis faced pressure for most of the game, getting sacked three times as rookie EDGE Derrick Moore picked up the first and second sacks of his NFL career.

When Willis had time to throw, he didn't look that good. He had some nice plays removed because of the offense's lack of discipline, but he was held to 128 passing yards and seven rushing yards. Lions safety Chuck Clark also picked him off, his second of the year.

Miami's penalties helped Detroit in a big way

While the Lions defense played well, they got bailed out a few times by the Dolphins' own mistakes. Whether it was a false start, offensive pass interference, or holding, the Dolphins kept shooting themselves in the foot. Willis had a great 50+ yard throw overturned for holding, and a few successful runs by Gordon were wiped away as well. If Detroit couldn't stop them, the Dolphins stopped themselves.

If Miami didn't get called for as many flags as they did, this game could've been a lot closer, or possibly Miami could've won this game. It's hard to win football games when you are beating yourself, and that is what Miami did, getting 11 penalties for 87 yards.

On offense, the Lions leaned on kicker Jake Bates. Bates made all four field goal attempts, the longest from 43 yards. He did make a mistake on kickoff where he didn't land it in the landing zone, but besides that, he was the best player for the Lions when it came to putting points on the board. It helps having a kicker you can rely on to put up points and make drives worthwhile when the offense can't find the end zone.

articles.title: Jordan Love's 100th career touchdown pass goes to Matthew Golden
articles.summary: The 100th career touchdown pass from Jordan Love went to Matthew Golden on a 5-yard score during Sunday's showdown with the Patriots.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love threw his 100th career touchdown pass on a 5-yard completion to Matthew Golden during the first quarter of Sunday's Week 9 showdown with the New England Patriots.

Love became the fifth Packers quarterback to reach 100 career touchdown passes, joining Bart Starr, Lynn Dickey, Brett Favre and Aaron Rodgers.

Love needed only 66 career games and 57 starts to get to 100. Rodgers got to 100 in 55 career starts; Favre needed 62. All three quarters were in Year 4 as starting quarterbacks in Green Bay when they reached 100 career touchdown passes.

Here's Love's milestone touchdown on Sunday in Foxborough:

On the scoring drive, Golden caught all three passes from Love, gaining 70 yards and finishing it off with the 5-yard touchdown.

Love has accounted for both of the Packers touchdowns to start Sunday, including a 13-yard touchdown run after Xavier McKinney's interception. Green Bay leads 14-0 in the first quarter.

articles.title: Josh Jacobs questionable to return with a hand injury
articles.summary: Packers running back Josh Jacobs may be done for the day in New England.
articles.body:
Packers running back Josh Jacobs may be done for the day in New England.

Jacobs went to the locker room during the Packers' third possession of the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Patriots. The Packers announced that he is considered questionable to return due to a hand injury.

Jacobs ran four times for five yards before heading inside. He got his hand caught in the facemask of Patriots safety Craig Woodson on one of those runs and it seems likely that's when he was injured.

MarShawn Lloyd is inactive, so Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson are the other available running backs for Green Bay. The Packers lead 14-0 with just over two minutes to play in the first quarter.

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau offers no regrets for joining LIV and no clear plans for his next step
articles.summary: DeChambeau and Jon Rahm, both two-time major champions, are the two biggest names in the rival league that no longer is supported by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia.
articles.body: Bryson DeChambeau offered no regrets for taking Saudi riches to join LIV Golf and no indication about his immediate future, saying only that he will approach it with “humility and respect for the game.” DeChambeau posted his thoughts on social media Sunday, his first public comments since LIV on Thursday abandoned plans to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy with a new version of the league. He had the most gravitas of any player supporting LIV 2.0. “I’m not going to rewrite the last four years,” DeChambeau wrote. “I made a decision I believed in, and I’m grateful for what came with it: playing in front of fans new and old around the world who rarely got to see the best players at home.” DeChambeau and Jon Rahm, both two-time major champions, are the two biggest names in the rival league that no longer is supported by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia. The bankruptcy court in New Jersey approved the end of Rahm’s contract with LIV. Rahm won the Abu Dhabi Championship on Sunday, moving him back into the top 10 in the world. The Spaniard has said he has not spoken to the PGA Tour about a path back — for now, he is looking at a European tour schedule for 2027 because the PGA Tour has banned LIV players for one year since their last appearance. DeChambeau’s case might be more complex because he was among the players who filed an antitrust lawsuit against the PGA Tour. He also said in a CNN interview after the June 2023 framework agreement among the PGA Tour, European tour and PIF: “It does stink from my perspective that the PGA Tour players are not necessarily winning. I hope they can find a way to make sure they are valued in the same way we are over at LIV.” “Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that along the way, I’ve said some things that didn’t help,” DeChambeau wrote in Sunday’s post. “Whatever comes next, I’ll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before me.” DeChambeau is scheduled to play the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa — site of his fifth and final LIV Golf victory — on Dec. 3-6 in Johannesburg. It will be only his third tournament outside of LIV and the majors since he left the PGA Tour in June 2022. “Beyond that, I’ll go about whatever is next the right way,” he said. DeChambeau, who led the Crushers to a season title in 2023, said he still believes in team golf beyond the Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup. “It may look different in the future, but I still believe it’s essential to growing the game,” he said.
